          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. In pursuance of our order passed yesterday, i.e.,
dated  29.07.2026,  Mr.  Guruprasad,  Principal  Secretary,
Housing and Development Authority, Government of U.P. has
joined the proceedings online. Mr. Nand Kishore Kalal,
Vice-Chairman,  Ghaziabad  Development  Authority  is
personally  present  in  the  Court  today.  Mr.  Kalal  is
represented today by Ms. Madhavi Divan, the learned senior
counsel.
2. We heard Ms. Dr. Menaka Guruswamy, the learned senior
counsel appearing for the home-buyers, Mr. Nikhil Goel, the
learned senior counsel appearing for the SRA and on the
other hand, today, we also have Mr. Vikas Singh, the
learned senior counsel appearing for the respondent no.3.
3. According to Dr. Menaka Guruswamy, the core issue that
falls for the consideration of this Court is whether the
Ghaziabad Development Authority (GDA) can lawfully continue
to withhold renewal of the development license and sanction
of the revised building plan and, thereby, stall the
implementation of the resolution plan already approved
under Section 31 of the IBC.
2

--- Page 200 ---
C.A. No.4473/2026
4. According to Dr. Guruswamy, the refusal at the end of
the GDA is on technical grounds. At this stage, we must
record what has been given to understand by Mr. Vikas
Singh,  the  learned  senior  counsel  appearing  for  the
respondent  no.3.  According  to  Mr.  Vikas  Singh,  the
development license is not in the name of the SRA. The
development license is in the name of the respondent no.3.
To put it briefly, what we have been given to understand by
Mr. Vikas Singh is that he holds the development license
for 99 acres. Whatever development has been undertaken is
on 26 acres of land. He is in possession of the balance
portion of the land in question and he also proposes to
develop the balance portion in future.
5. Mr. Singh does not dispute the fact that few towers
have come up on the land admeasuring 26 acres. According to
him, whatever construction has come up is in a very
dilapidated condition today. He has many proposals to put
forward with respect to the development of this 26 acres of
land also. At this point of time, we do not want to say
anything in this regard.
6. Today, all that we intend to do is to direct the State
of U.P. and the GDA to sit together and take one final
decision  with  regard  to  the  development  license  and
sanction of the revised building plans. To put it in other
words, whatever proposal has been forwarded by the GDA to
the State should be discussed at the earliest and a
3

--- Page 201 ---
C.A. No.4473/2026
reasoned order needs to be passed at the end of it with
regard to what we have observed aforesaid.
7. Let this exercise be undertaken at the earliest and an
appropriate decision be placed before this Court within a
period of two weeks from today. Once we are in receipt of
the final decision that the Government would take in
consultation with the GDA, we shall, thereafter proceed to
discuss further issues.
8. We impress upon Sh. Guruprasad as well as Sh. Kalal to
have a thorough inspection of the entire site in question.
They should visit the site with surveyors and officers who
are experts in preparing sketches.
9. It shall be ensured that the 26 acres can be made
habitable and access can be ensured without impinging upon
the balance properties which is in the possession of the
respondent no.3.
10. If the State and the GDA wants any assistance or any
further information from the parties concerned, it shall be
open for them to call them. We make it further clear that
the inspection shall be in the presence of all the parties
concerned.
11. Post the matter on 20.08.2026.
(HARPREET KAUR)                                 (POOJA SHARMA)
COURT MASTER (SH)                             COURT MASTER (NSH)

1. Heard Mr.Jaideep Gupta learned Senior Counsel for
the appellants and Mr.G.Umapathy, learned Senior Counsel
for the State of Tamil Nadu.
2. Learned Senior Counsel for the appellants-Mr.Jaideep
Gupta’s principal submission is that, the registration of
a  Suo  Motu case  was  beyond  the  jurisdiction  of  the
National  Green  Tribunal,  Southern  Zone,  Chennai  (for
short, ‘NGT’). According to learned Senior Counsel for the
appellants, being an  inter-state water dispute, Article
262 of the Constitution of India read with Section 6(A)
further read with Section 11 of the Inter-State River

--- Page 211 ---
2
Water  Disputes  Act,  1956  would  bar  the  NGT  from
entertaining and deciding the controversy.
3. We  are  of  the  opinion  that  since  the  impugned
order(s) is only an order taking suo motu cognizance and
issuance of notice, these objections can be raised before
the  NGT  itself  and  the  relevant  constitutional  and
statutory  provisions  be  pointed  out  before  the  NGT.
Learned Senior Counsel for the appellants also submits
that on the aspect of jurisdiction, the matter is settled
by the judgments of this Court.
4. We permit the appellants to raise this issue before
the NGT and point out the constitutional and statutory
provisions before the NGT. The State of Tamil Nadu also
would be at liberty to point out its objections to the
submission of the State of Kerala.
5. In the event of any adverse order being passed, the
appellants will have liberty to challenge the present
impugned order(s) as well as the order(s) which is made
hereinafter.
6. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that, at
the outset, the State will make an application before the
NGT on the preliminary jurisdiction objections.
7. If such an application is made, the same shall be
decided first on its own merits, uninfluenced by any of
the observations in the impugned orders or in this order.
8. The appeals are disposed of in the above terms.

disposed of.

1. Leave granted.
2. This appeal challenges the order of the
High Court affirming the conviction of the
petitioner under Section 6 of the Protection
of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
(POCSO) and Section 506 of the Indian Penal
Code, 1860 (IPC), under which he was sentenced
to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period
of twenty years.
3. We have heard learned counsel for the
parties and carefully perused the material
placed on record.
4. At this stage, without expressing any
final opinion on the merits, we find that the
present petition raises substantial arguable
issues of discrepancies in the USG gestational
age report, the admitted prior relationship
SLP (Crl.) No.6755/2026      2

--- Page 220 ---
between the parties, whether the victim is a
minor, unexplained delay in filing the FIR,
and age determination in the absence of an
ossification test.
5. Having regard to the totality of the
circumstances,  particularly  the  substantial
period of incarceration (8 years) undergone,
the possibility of consideration of appeal,
and the serious arguable issues raised, we are
satisfied that a clear case for suspension of
sentence during the pendency of the appeal is
made out.
6. Accordingly,  the  execution  of  the
sentence  imposed  upon  the  appellant  shall
remain suspended during the pendency of the
appeal.
7. The appellant is ordered to be released
on bail, subject to terms and conditions that
the trial court may deem fit and proper to

impose.

1. These petitions are filed seeking transfer of the proceedings
bearing Criminal M.A. No.1143 of 2023 and R.C.C. No.620 of 2024,
pending before the Court of the 6 th Civil Judge (Senior Division),
and CJM at Panvel, Maharashtra, to a Court having competent
jurisdiction at Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu.
2. The grounds raised by the petitioners for seeking the transfer
are that they are aged senior citizens suffering from serious
medical ailments and are unable to undertake repeated travel to
Panvel;  and  respondents  are  at  present  residing  abroad  and
prosecuting the proceedings through a Power of Attorney/counsel, no
prejudice would be caused by the said transfer.
3. On such consideration, we are of the view that the transfer
can be allowed. Consequently, the Transfer Petitions are allowed.  
4. Accordingly, the proceedings bearing Criminal M.A. No.1143 of
2023 and R.C.C. No.620 of 2024, pending before the Court of the 6 th
Civil Judge (Senior Division) and CJM at Panvel, Maharashtra, are

and the High Courts of India has filed the instant writ petition  
under Article 32 of the Constitution of India, inter alia, seeking 

--- Page 227 ---
2
the following reliefs:
“A. Issue appropriate writ, order or direction to the  
Respondents to apply the amended Rule 3B of Supreme  
Court Judges Rules, to the spouse of the deceased Judge  
of the Supreme Court also;
B. Issue appropriate writ, order or direction to the  
Respondents  to  consider  the  representation  dated  
01.07.2022 and 18.03.2025 and take appropriate steps for  
amendment in the High Court Judges Rules, 1956 in terms  
of the said Representations.

Respondents to grant the post retiral benefits to former  
judges of the Hon'ble Supreme Court and Hon'ble High  
Courts  as  per  the  Petitioner  Association's  
representations dated 01.07.2022 and 18.03.2025.
D. Issue appropriate writ, order or direction to the  
Respondents to appropriately amend the service Rules of  
Judges of the Hon'ble Supreme Court and Hon'ble High  
Courts in order to bring uniformity in grant of post  
retiral and medical benefits;
E. Pass any other appropriate writ order or direction as  
this Hon'ble Court may deem fit and proper in the facts  
and circumstances of the case”
2. It appears that a comprehensive representation has been made  
by the petitioner-Association to the Government of India, raising  
these issues, especially the purported omission of the expression  
“spouse” in Rule 3-B of the Supreme Court Judges Rules 1959. It  
goes without saying that the non-inclusion of “spouse and/or  
dependent-children” within the said Rule deserves to be examined by  
the Competent Authority for taking an appropriate decision. In any  
event, such issue can be effectively considered by the Committee  
that the Government of India has fairly agreed to constitute in  
terms of this Court’s order dated 20.07.2026 passed in Contempt  
Petition (C) Nos. 425-426/2015 in W.P. (C) No. 523/2022.

representations dated 01.07.2022 and 18.03.2025 submitted by the  
petitioner-Association  and  refer  all  the  pending  issues  for  
consideration of the Committee, referred to hereinabove.
4. The pending applications, if any, also stand disposed of.

offence of murder punishable under Section 302 of the
1

--- Page 233 ---
SLP (CRL.)D.No.9856/2026
Indian Penal Code (for short, “the IPC”) along with other
co-accused.
6. It is very disturbing to note that although the
incident is of the year 1981 yet the judgment and order
passed by the Trial Court holding the petitioner guilty of
the alleged crime is of the year 2002.
7. We fail to understand, why it took 22 years for the
Trial Court to complete the trial.
8. Besides the above, we are also disturbed to note that
the further statement of the petitioner under Section 313
of  the  Cr.P.C.  was  recorded  in  the  year  1994  and,
thereafter, the judgment was delivered in the year 2002.

decide the appeal preferred by the petitioner challenging
the judgment and order of conviction passed by the Trial
Court.
10. This  delay  highlighted  above  is  something  very
disturbing.
11. We would like to have a comprehensive report in this
regard from the State as well as the High Court, more
particularly, why it took these many years to complete the
trial and decide the criminal appeal.
12. The learned counsel further pointed out that his
client,  as  on  date  is  almost  70  years  of  age  with

THE STATE OF HARYANA & ANR.                        RESPONDENT(S)
O R D E R
1. Leave granted. 
2. The present appeal has been filed against the impugned
order dated 27.03.2025 passed by the High Court of Punjab
and Haryana, wherein, the appellants had preferred a
petition under Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik
Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 seeking the prayer to quash the
FIR No. 147/2024 dated 23.07.2024 registered at Police
Station -  Thanesar, District – Kurukshetra, Haryana for
the  offences  punishable  under  Sections
316(2),318(4),338,336(3),340(2),351(2),351(3), 61(2) and
238 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (for short,
‘BNS’) and subsequent proceedings emanating therefrom.
3. The appellants had filed the aforesaid petition on the
strength of a compromise dated 23.10.2024 entered between
them and the complainant, i.e., respondent no. 2. The
High Court vide the impugned order dismissed the petition

--- Page 263 ---
2
noting that only four out of the six accused persons had
preferred  the  petition  seeking  quashing  of  criminal
proceedings, and in such view of the matter, piecemeal
settlement in a criminal case would not be permissible,
as such a situation would hinder joint trials. 
4. We have heard the learned counsel appearing for the
parties and perused the records.
5. Taking note of the compromise dated 23.10.2024 (Annexure
P-2) entered into the between the appellant and the
private respondent, the proceedings before the Trial
Court  qua the appellants alone, stands quashed. The
compromise dated 23.10.2024 shall form part and parcel of
this order. 
6. We make it clear that criminal proceedings shall continue
against the other accused persons, who have not preferred
any appeal before us.
7. The appeal stands disposed of, in the aforesaid terms,
accordingly. 
8. Pending application(s), if any, shall also stand disposed
of.

Leave granted.
The  appellant  stands  convicted  for  the
offences  punishable  under  Section  6  of  the
Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act,
2012 and Section 506 of the Indian Penal Code,
1860 by the Trial Court and has been sentenced to
undergo imprisonment for life. The High Court was
pleased to dismiss his appeal against conviction.
Hence, the present appeal. 
We have heard the learned counsel appearing
for the parties.
Admittedly,  the  appellant  has  been  under
incarceration for nearly 6 years. W e do find the
existence of arguable issues in the appeal both on
facts and law.
Suffice  it  is  to  state  that  continued
incarceration of the appellant is not required,

--- Page 276 ---
3
especially when the appellant was a young man at
the time when the offence is said to have been
committed.
In such view of the matter, we are inclined
to suspend the sentence and grant bail to the
appellant, during the pendency of the appeal.
Accordingly, the sentence of the appellant is
suspended and he is granted bail, during the
pendency of the present appeal, on terms and
conditions to the satisfaction of the concerned
Trial Court.

M/S CHIRAG CONSTRUCTION & ANR.          APPELLANTS
                                VERSUS
RESOLUTION PROFESSIONAL OF ANUDAN PROPERTIES 
PRIVATE LIMITED & ORS.                               RESPONDENTS
O R D E R
Despite the Civil Appeal having been filed nearly one and a
half years ago, the appellants have not served the caveator till
date. 
Today, Mr. Aditya Giri, learned Advocate-on-Record has entered
appearance on behalf of the appellants and states that he has
recently  been  engaged.  He  prays  for  some  time  to  file  a
supplementary affidavit to bring on record subsequent events.
When asked what are the subsequent events, he states that he
has no knowledge of the same. 
Keeping in view the fact that for the last one and a half
years the appellants have not served the caveator, this Court is of
the view that there has been negligence in pursuing the present
matter.

--- Page 296 ---
2
 Accordingly, the present appeal is dismissed in default and
on account of non-prosecution.

judgment will operate prospectively, the impugned order
deserves to be stayed and is accordingly stayed.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. The present petition has been filed being aggrieved
by the order dated 11.03.2025, passed by the High Court of
Judicature for Rajasthan at Jodhpur in SBCRMP No. 1634 of
2018 preferred under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal
Procedure, 1973 (for short ‘Cr.P.C.’), for quashing of FIR
No. 113 dated 02.04.2009 registered at P.S. Sardarshahar,
District Churu for the offences punishable under Sections
420, 467, 468, 471 and 120B IPC.
2. The present case has got a checkered history, and
proceedings were initiated on the basis of aforesaid FIR.
3. Earlier also, an attempt was made by the petitioner
for quashing of the proceedings by filing a petition under
Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. However, it was disposed of by
granting  a  liberty  to  the  petitioners  to  prefer  a
representation  before  the  investigating  authority,
including the facts of ongoing civil litigations between
the parties.
4. A detailed representations was preferred in the
matter  as  directed  by  the  High  Court,  and  as  the
representation  was  rejected,  a  second  petition  was
preferred under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C.
5. The High Court has dismissed the second petition
preferred under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C.
6. In the considered opinion of this Court, as it was a
2

--- Page 312 ---
second petition preferred under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C.,
the High Court ought to have decided the matter on merits
after going through the entire record produced by the
parties.
7. As the matter was not decided on merits, the matter
is remanded back to the High Court to hear all the parties
and to decide the matter in accordance with law on the
basis of documents produced by the parties in the matter on
merits.
8. A request is also made to the High Court to decide
the matter at an early date as expeditiously as possible.
9. With  the  above  observation,  the  Special  Leave
Petition stands disposed of.
10. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed
of.

For Respondent(s) 
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Refiling delay condoned.
2. This petition seeks leave to impugn order
1

--- Page 332 ---
dated 22.04.2026 passed by the High Court of
Judicature at Madras in C.R.P. No. 2409/2026
whereby the revision of the petitioner against
the  order  of  First  Appellate  Court  allowing
defendant’s  application  to  submit  additional
documents, has been dismissed.
3. The submission on behalf of the petitioner
is that while admitting additional evidence, the
Court’s power is circumscribed by the limit set
out in Order 41 Rule 27 of the Code of Civil
Procedure, 1973 and those limits have been given
a go-bye by the First Appellate Court while
admitting additional evidence.
4. Without expressing any opinion on the merits
of the aforesaid submission, we are of the view
that ends of justice would be served if we
permit the petitioner to raise these grounds in
a Second Appeal in the event of there being a
decision  against  the  appellant  in  the  First
Appeal.
5. We, accordingly, dispose of this petition by
observing that in the event the First Appeal is
decided  against  the  petitioner  and  a  Second
Appeal is preferred by the petitioner against
2

--- Page 333 ---
the order of the First Appellate Court, it will
be open for the petitioner to raise the issue of
admission of additional evidence and take it as
a ground to challenge the order of the First
Appellate  Court.  In  such  eventuality,  the
impugned order of the High Court rejecting the
revision shall not come in the way.
6. With the aforesaid observations, the special
leave petition stands disposed of.
7. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand
disposed of.

Application  seeking  oral  hearing  of  the  Review
Petition is rejected.
The office report dated 22 June 2026 indicates that
the  Review  Petition  is  defective  for  the  reasons
mentioned therein. Despite Registry's communication, the
learned counsel for the petitioners has not cured the
defects.
That apart, there is an inordinate delay of 265 days
in filing the present Review Petition, for which no
satisfactory  explanation  has  been  offered  by  the
petitioners.
Thus, though the present Review Petition is liable to
be dismissed on the ground of delay itself, yet we have
carefully gone through the Review Petition and the papers
connected therewith. We are satisfied that no case for
review of this Court's order dated 17.07.2025, dismissing
the Special Leave Petition, has been made out.
The Review Petition is, accordingly, dismissed on the
ground of delay as well as on merits.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. The petitioner was denied anticipatory bail by the High Court
in connection with FIR No. 98/2023 registered with the Police
Station PS Women, Patiala by his wife for the offences punishable
under Sections 498-A and 406 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC).

--- Page 683 ---
2
2. By our Order issuing notice, we had granted protection to the
petitioner from any coercive steps and directed the parties to
appear before the Supreme Court Mediation Centre for the purpose of
exploring an amicable settlement. It has come to our notice that
the said mediation proceedings have failed. 
3. The learned counsel appearing for the State had brought to our
notice  that  the  petitioner  has  been  cooperating  in  the
investigation. Furthermore, by our previous order in this matter
dated 16-07-2026, we had directed the petitioner to deposit the
arrears of maintenance due to the wife. The Petitioner has complied
with the same by transferring an amount of Rs. 2,65,000/- to the
wife. 
4. Thus, we are of the opinion that the petitioner can be
released  on  anticipatory  bail,  on  condition  that  he  shall
co-operate  with  the  investigation  and  duly  pay  the  interim
maintenance, of Rs.10,000/- per month, which is fixed by the
learned Magistrate under the Protection of Women from Domestic
Violence Act, 2005, before the 5th of every month, subject only to
setoff on the final determination of maintenance.  
5. We order that on the appearance of the petitioner before the
IO in the event of his in connection with the offences enumerated
above, he shall be released on bail, subject to the terms and
conditions that the I.O. may deem fit to impose.
6. Once the petitioner is released on bail by the I.O., on
directions  issued  by  the  I.O.  or  summons  issued  by  the
jurisdictional Court, the petitioner shall appear before the Trial
Court and furnish fresh bail bonds and ensure due appearance in the
trial.
7. With the aforesaid, this petition stands disposed of.
8. Pending applications, if any, also stand disposed of.

1

the petitioner at her house. Later, the differences
were resolved and an affidavit was presented by the
prosecutirxbefore  the  High  Court  agreeing  for
quashment  of  the  FIR  and  the  consequential
proceedings as they were instituted on account of
some misunderstanding between them.

High Court declined the prayer to quash the FIR.  
3. The submission on behalf of the petitioner is
that this is not a case of usual rape but it is a
case of alleged physical relationship between two
persons who were formally engaged to get married
and, therefore, basis a settlement, the proceedings
can be quashed to ensure that there is no abuse of
the process of law.  Moreover, it is a case where
the prosecutrix herself would be the witness and if
she is not wiling to come forward, the trial would
be an exercise in futility.

accepted by Mr. Jogy Scaria, AOR
